stage_a.note: High energy, big smiles and enthusiastic delivery throughout the presentation.
Animated gestures and excited tone when describing the product's features.
Friendly, engaging eye contact and warm smiles directed at the panel.

venture.description: Stick-on, rechargeable wall sconces that install without tools or wiring and are app-controlled.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces herself as Caroline.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Introduces herself as Rose, states they are a wife and wife duo, and gives their ask.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they needed to install wall lights when they moved in together.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Notes that installing wall lighting is a hassle even if you are handy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Describes the difficulties of punching holes, running wires, and patching drywall.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mentions that hiring an electrician can cost over a thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokes about the cost in this economy.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains they wanted a better way, leading to their lightbulb moment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Invites the sharks to see how it is done.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Introduces Poplight as modern, stylish wall lighting that is easy to install and remove.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shows how it installs in seconds using double-sided adhesive with no tools.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Points out the built-in level on the base to ensure it is straight.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Remarks that the built-in level is cool.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Demonstrates swiveling and clicking the light into place.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses pleasant surprise at how simple it is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Adds that the light is dimmable.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Playfully acts as if Lori asked how it is powered.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it is USB-C rechargeable and the battery can be popped out to charge.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Jokes with Kevin that getting up to adjust lighting is not an executive move.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces the app to change color warmth, set timers, and dim the light.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States Poplight is designed for everyone, from homeowners to dorm rooms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks who is ready to revolutionize wall lighting.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Invites the panel to check out the samples in front of them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what happens to the wall when the adhesive is removed.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains that the design ensures removing the tape leaves no damage on the wall.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks where the button is to turn the light on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Directs him to look at the bottom and tap the small power button.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Acknowledges finding the button.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks for the retail price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the retail price is 95 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what it costs to make.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Breaks down the cost to make, landed cost, retail price, and calculates the profit margin.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if they will sell direct to consumer only.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Suggests that the price point is kind of expensive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that tests showed customers were more responsive to a higher price with a discount.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: States he does not think 95 dollars is expensive.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks how long the battery charge lasts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Provides the charging time and the estimated battery life depending on brightness.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if there are other adhesive-backed tap lights out there.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Claims it did not exist and they have three patents on the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what the patents cover.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Lists a design patent and two pending patents on the technology.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Details that the patents cover the swivel mechanism and how the tape attaches to the base.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if they have sold any units.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mentions they launched a successful Kickstarter earlier in the year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks them to provide more details about the Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reports raising over $178k in under 4 weeks and hitting their goal rapidly.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if their current inventory is just to fulfill the Kickstarter orders.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if they have shipped any of the Kickstarter orders yet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Confirms they have not shipped yet.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if there are orders outside of the crowdfunding campaign.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they launched a website and credits Rose as the social media queen.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Adds that they went viral on TikTok and sales have been organic.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks for the specific sales figures generated online after Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reveals they have made about 5,000 dollars since the website went live.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Guesses that both founders still hold other jobs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Confirms they have full time jobs which help fund the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what their backgrounds are and what they do.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Shares her background in tech startups and her family history of entrepreneurship.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains her job as a clinical social worker and her interest in figuring out how things work.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Makes an offer involving equity and a royalty structure, citing the nascent stage of the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Jokes about expecting a royalty and being shocked he didn't ask for a piece of their marriage.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Tells the founders that Kevin's offer is a really good deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Presents a simple offer with no equity but a high royalty per unit in perpetuity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Expresses shock at the high royalty amount proposed by Barbara.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Exits, stating he loves the product but thinks Kevin's offer is strong enough.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Exits due to concerns about competition in the stick-on lighting marketplace.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Exits, unconvinced because removing hidden tape might still be a battle.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Urges the founders to focus on the standing deals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks Barbara if she would consider a lower royalty.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what royalty amount they feel they can afford.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Suggests a 12 dollar royalty would be more comfortable.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Revises her offer to include cash, a credit line, and the requested lower royalty.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Pressures the founders to make a decision.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Counters Kevin's offer by asking to lower the royalty cap.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Refuses the counter, stating his original offer is fair and has no wiggle room.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts Kevin's standing offer.

decisions.terms: $150k for 8% with a $2 royalty until $500k is paid, then $1 in perpetuity
decisions.note: Thinks the business is very nascent and a crapshoot.

decisions.terms: $150k for 0% equity, with a $20 royalty per unit in perpetuity
decisions.note: Wants a simple offer without taking equity.
Loves the product and founders but thinks Kevin's offer is good and Barbara's is nuts.
Concerned about competition in the stick-on lighting marketplace.
Thinks removing the tape will be a battle and is not convinced it's a win.

decisions.terms: $100k cash and $50k credit line for a $12 royalty per unit in perpetuity
decisions.note: Counters founder's request to lower the $20 royalty.
Asks Kevin to lower the royalty cap.
Agrees to the deal after Kevin refuses to lower the cap.

record.notes: The founders present a highly energetic pitch. Minor interruptions during the presentation by Mark and Barbara are recorded as accepts turns.
